title: What If Everyone Over 18 Disappeared Overnight?

shots.vo: One morning, every person over eighteen was gone. Every single one.

shots.label: MONDAY, 9:47 AM
shots.vo: Zoe woke up two hours late. No alarm. No mom yelling. Nothing.
Mom? Why didn't you wake me up? I'm so late!
The kitchen was empty. Coffee still warm. Mom's phone on the table. Her shoes by the door.
Zoe? I can't find Mom. Or Dad. Their car is still here.
Theo. Her little brother. Eight years old. Holding his stuffed shark like his life depended on it.

shots.label: OUTSIDE
shots.vo: Outside, the street was full of cars. Stopped in the middle of the road. Doors open. Engines running.
No drivers. No adults anywhere. Just kids. Standing in the street. Confused.
Zoe! Yo! Are your parents gone too?
My mom, my uncle, the mailman. The bus driver! The bus is just sitting there!
Rico. Her best friend. Seventeen. Same as her.
Zoe tried calling her mom. Then 911. Then anyone.
So, no adults. No school. No rules. Am I the only one who thinks this is kind of awesome?
Rico. Theo is eight. Who's going to take care of the little kids?
Then every phone in the street buzzed at the same time.
A voice message. Sent to every number in town.

messages.text: Everyone come to Lincoln High. Now.

shots.vo: Blake Hart. The mayor's son. Of course.
The adults were gone. And someone had already decided he was the new boss.
Every adult in town vanished overnight. The mayor's son just declared himself in charge.

shots.label: LINCOLN HIGH
shots.vo: Two thousand kids packed into the school gym. Some crying. Some cheering. Most just scared.
Listen up! The adults are gone. Nobody knows why. But someone has to lead. And that's me.
Rule one. No school. Rule two. Everything in the stores is free. Rule three. Have fun.
The gym exploded. Two thousand kids screaming his name.
Free stores? That food has to last us. Nobody's making more.
Two thousand kids. The supermarkets have maybe two weeks of food. If nobody wastes it.

shots.label: DAY 1, AFTERNOON
shots.vo: Nobody wasted it. They destroyed it.
Zoe, relax! It's day one! The adults will probably be back by tonight!

shots.label: DAY 1, EVENING
shots.vo: They weren't back by tonight. Lena had an idea. Drive to the next town and get help.
They reached the edge of town. The sign said, Thank you for visiting. Sam hit the gas.
And the car stopped. Like it hit a wall made of glass.
There was an invisible wall around the whole town. Nobody could get out. And nobody was coming in.

shots.label: THE SUPERMARKET
shots.vo: Zoe went to get more food. But the supermarket doors were locked. And guarded.
Sorry, Zoe. New rule. Food goes through me now.
My team gets fed first. Then whoever helps my team. You want food? Work for me.
I have twenty three little kids at my house. They don't work for anybody.
Blake thought about it. Then he handed her one bag. One.

shots.label: DAY 2, NIGHT
shots.vo: That night, Zoe was walking home when the streetlights flickered.
Once. Twice. Then the whole town went black.
No power plant workers meant no power. And two thousand kids were about to find out what that meant.
No adults. No way out. And now the power is gone too.
The scream came from the park. Zoe ran toward it with her phone flashlight.
A kid had fallen off the playground. Broken arm. And there was no hospital. No doctor.
Move. I did a first aid course. Twice. I can splint it.
We can't keep doing this, Lena. We need power. We need a hospital. We need a plan.
I can get the power back. Maybe. My dad works at the plant. Worked. I've seen the control room.

shots.label: POWER PLANT
shots.vo: The power plant. Two in the morning. Three teenagers and a flashlight.
Okay. Big red button probably means bad. Small green button probably means... good?
He pressed it. The whole building hummed to life.
Across town, the lights came back on. Two thousand kids cheered.
Then every screen in the control room turned on at once. All of them showing the same thing.
A number. Eighteen.
Eighteen. Like the age. Everyone over eighteen vanished.
They watched it. For a full minute. Then a minute more.

shots.label: 3:00 AM
shots.vo: At three a.m. exactly, it changed. Seventeen.
It's not an age. It's a countdown. Seventeen days left.
Seventeen days until something happened. And nobody knew what.
A countdown appeared on every screen in town. Seventeen days. Until what?
I know what it means. When it hits zero, everyone who's turned eighteen by then disappears too.
Panic. Seniors started crying. Some started running.
So we need order. Real order. From now on, I make the rules. And my team enforces them.
Behind him, twenty seniors put on red armbands. Blake's Guard.

shots.label: THAT EVENING
shots.vo: That night, Rico came over. He was quiet. Rico was never quiet.
Zoe. What's the date tomorrow?
Zoe counted in her head. Then her stomach dropped.
Your birthday. You turn eighteen tomorrow.
If Blake is right... I'm not making it to the countdown. I'm gone at midnight.

shots.label: 11:59 PM
shots.vo: Eleven fifty nine. Zoe, Rico, Theo, Lena and Sam. Holding hands. Watching the clock.
Midnight.
One second. Two seconds. Nothing happened.
Then Zoe noticed Rico's hand. She could see the couch through it.
He looked down. He was fading. Slowly. Like a ghost in daylight.
Zoe. Listen to me. Take care of Theo. Don't let Blake win. And don't cry, it's my birthday.
Rico! No! Hold on!
Her hands closed around nothing.
Rico was gone.

shots.label: 3:14 AM
shots.vo: Nobody slept. At three fourteen, Rico's phone lit up on the floor. Where he had been standing.
A message. From Rico's own number.

messages.text: im ok. im not dead. everyone is here

shots.vo: Rico was alive. The adults were alive. Somewhere. And the countdown was a lie.
Rico vanished on his eighteenth birthday. Hours later, he texted: everyone is alive. Don't trust the countdown.

shots.label: DAY 6
shots.vo: I traced the message. It didn't come from outside the wall. It came from inside town.
The old radio tower. On the hill. Past the woods.
That's in the North Zone. Blake made it off limits on day three. Anyone caught there loses their food.
Then we don't get caught. We go tonight.
Theo. You stay here with the little kids. Lock the door. Don't open it for anyone.
What if you disappear too?
I'm seventeen, buddy. I've got a whole year. Pinky promise.

shots.label: NORTH ZONE
shots.vo: Midnight. They crept past Blake's guards. Through the woods. Up the hill.

shots.label: RADIO TOWER
shots.vo: The radio tower. Its red light was blinking. It shouldn't have power. Nothing up here did.
Inside, a radio was crackling. And through the static, a voice.
Zoe? Zoe, sweetheart, can you hear me?
Mom? Mom! Where are you?!
We don't know. It's white. Everywhere. We can't move. We can only hear you. Zoe, listen. It's not a countdown.
Then the static swallowed her voice. And the radio went dead.
Behind them, a metal door creaked open. It led underground. And painted on it were two words.
Day zero.
Zoe heard her mom through a radio. The adults are trapped somewhere white. And there's a door marked day zero.

shots.label: UNDERGROUND
shots.vo: Behind the door, stairs. Down and down. Into a room full of screens.
Every screen showed the same thing. A white room. Endless. And thousands of people. Standing still.
There. That's my mom. And there's Rico. Next to her.
One page. A few lines. They read it together.
The young will choose? Choose what?
Before anyone could answer, flashlights hit them from the stairs.
Well. Look who decided to break the rules.
Blake. You knew about this place. Didn't you?
Because some of us don't want our parents back, Zoe.
Take them. Lock them up. They've seen too much.

shots.label: SCHOOL OFFICE
shots.vo: Blake locked Zoe in the principal's office. Lena and Sam in the library. Separated.
My dad is the mayor. Everyone thinks he's great. At home, nothing I do is ever good enough.
Six days without him and I'm finally someone. People listen to me. Why would I bring him back?
Because Theo is eight and he cries himself to sleep. Because this isn't about you.

shots.label: DAY 7, EVENING
shots.vo: Hours passed. Then a scratching sound. From the air vent.
Room service. Hurry. I've got maybe five minutes before the guard shift changes.
She's out. She went to your house to check on the kids. But Zoe... she just texted me.
Sam held up his phone.

messages.text: kids are here. all of them. except one

shots.vo: Theo. Theo's gone?
Which means someone took him.
Zoe climbed into the vent. Blake could keep the town. But nobody touches her brother.
Zoe escaped from Blake's prison. Her eight year old brother Theo is missing.

shots.label: DAY 7, NIGHT
shots.vo: Zoe searched every street. The school. The playground. The ice cream shop he loved.
Theo! Theo, where are you?!
Zoe! Over here! The park! Look at the park!
The park was glowing. Lanterns everywhere. Tents. Blankets. A whole little city.
Hundreds of little kids. Seven, eight, nine years old. Sharing food. Taking care of each other.
Zoe! You came! Welcome to Kid City! I'm the mayor!
Zoe grabbed him and didn't let go for a full minute.
Don't you ever, ever do that again. Who told you to come here?
The man in white. He comes in my dreams. He said the little kids should be together. For the choice.
The choice? Theo, what choice?
Theo pulled a crumpled drawing out of his pocket. Crayon. A radio tower. A clock. And a lot of stick figures holding hands.
Underneath, in wobbly letters, five words.
The young will choose. And everyone has to agree. It's a vote.
A vote. When the countdown ends, every kid in town decides. Adults back. Or gone forever.
And the man said one more thing. If it's not everyone... it doesn't count.
Every kid in town had to agree. Including the one who wanted the adults gone forever.
To bring the adults back, every kid in town has to agree. Every single one. Even Blake.

shots.label: DAY 9
shots.vo: Zoe walked into Blake's gym. In front of everyone. With a crayon drawing.
The adults aren't dead. They're frozen. Under the radio tower. And when the countdown ends, we vote. Bring them back or lose them forever.
Or. Hear me out. We vote no.
No curfew. No homework. No one telling you who to be. Ever again. Raise your hand if you miss being grounded.

shots.label: THE CAMPAIGN
shots.vo: For the next three days, the town split in two. Team Zoe. Team Blake.

shots.label: DAY 12
shots.vo: I hacked into the vote counter. It's live. It shows who's leaning which way.
They looked at the screen together.
Twelve hundred no. We're losing. Badly.
Because Blake is selling them a party. And I'm selling them homework. We need to show them what they're really choosing.
The screens under the tower. If I can connect them to every TV in town...
Across town, every screen flickered. And there they were.
The white room. Thousands of parents. Frozen. Some of them crying. Frozen mid-tear.
They're not gone. They're waiting. And they can hear every word we say. Even this.
I'm not asking you to miss homework. I'm asking if you want to see your mom again.
On Sam's screen, the numbers started moving. Fast.
Then every screen in town went black.
He cut the power. Blake cut the power to the whole town.
That broadcast was fake. Zoe's trying to scare you. The adults aren't coming back. Ever.

shots.label: MIDNIGHT
shots.vo: At midnight, Zoe got a note. Slipped under her door. Neat handwriting.
The roof of the school. Tonight. Come alone. Blake.
Blake shut down the whole town to stop Zoe's broadcast. Now he wants to meet her alone.

shots.label: SCHOOL ROOF
shots.vo: The school roof. The whole town dark below them. Blake was sitting on the edge.
Did you see him? In the broadcast. My dad. Third row.
He was crying. My dad doesn't cry. Not at Grandma's funeral. Not ever. But he was crying.
What if he's crying because I'm not there? What if he actually... misses me?
But I don't think he meant beat you. I think he meant don't let the scared version of you win.
Bring him back, Blake. And then make him see you. For real this time.
Okay. I'll turn the power back on. And I'll tell them the truth. Tomorrow.
Then the radio tower on the hill lit up. Bright white. Brighter than the sun.
The countdown had jumped. Not four days. One hour.

shots.label: 59 MINUTES
shots.vo: Every kid in town ran to the gym. Two thousand. Packed shoulder to shoulder.
Everybody. I lied. The broadcast was real. Our parents are alive. And I was scared to get mine back.
I'm voting yes. And I'm asking you to vote yes with me.

shots.label: 30 MINUTES
shots.vo: Yes climbed fast. Fifteen hundred. Eighteen hundred. Nineteen fifty.

shots.label: 10 MINUTES
shots.vo: Then it stopped. Nineteen ninety nine yes. One no. And the no wouldn't change.
I can trace it. Give me a second. It's... it's coming from your phone, Zoe.
Zoe's phone. In her pocket. Except it wasn't in her pocket. Theo had it.

shots.label: 5 MINUTES
shots.vo: If they come back... will Kid City end? Will everyone forget we took care of each other?
Theo. You ran a whole city. You're the bravest person I know. That doesn't disappear when Mom comes home.
Pinky promise.
Ten seconds left. Theo pressed the button.
Two thousand yes. Zero no. And the whole world turned white.
Two thousand kids voted yes. Every single one. And the world turned white.

shots.label: MONDAY, 7:00 AM
shots.vo: Zoe opened her eyes. Her bedroom. Her alarm. Going off at seven a.m.
Zoe! Up! You're going to be late for school!
She ran downstairs. Mom was making coffee. Like nothing ever happened.
Zoe hugged her so hard the coffee spilled.
Whoa! Okay! I love you too? It's been one night, honey. Did you have a bad dream?
One night. For the adults, it had been one night. They didn't remember anything.
Zoe! Kid City is still in the park! The tents are still there! It was real!

shots.label: LINCOLN HIGH
shots.vo: Zoe! I'm back, baby! Eighteen and fabulous! Did anyone save me cake?
Every kid remembered. Every adult forgot. And every kid decided to keep it that way.

shots.label: CITY HALL
shots.vo: Across town, the mayor stood on the steps of city hall. His son walked up to him.
Dad. I need to tell you something. And I need you to actually listen.
His dad looked at him for a long time. Then he did something he'd never done. He sat down on the steps. And listened.

shots.label: THAT EVENING
shots.vo: That evening, Theo showed Zoe one last drawing. The man in white. Smiling.
He said thank you. He said it's a test. Every town gets one. Most towns vote no.
And what happens to the towns that vote no?
He didn't say. But he said he's going to visit another town tonight.
Maybe yours. If every adult in your town disappeared tonight... how would you vote?
